matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick reposition
matchstick.principle: A V (two diagonal sticks) can be turned into an X (two crossing diagonals) by moving one diagonal stick, and vice‑versa, changing the numeral’s value between 5 and 10.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a V or X and the numeric gap suggests a change of ±5, consider a single diagonal stick move between them.

matchstick.title: Check numeric discrepancy to guide stick moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides; the difference indicates how much the total must increase or decrease, guiding which characters to modify.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, after translating the Roman numerals to Arabic numbers.
matchstick.example: In ‘IX = XII + IV’, LHS=9, RHS=16, discrepancy=7, so the move must reduce RHS by 7 or raise LHS by 7.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign integrity
matchstick.principle: The ‘=’ sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; it cannot be altered, used as a source, or become another symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the puzzle; never select a stick from the equality sign for relocation.
matchstick.example: Never turn ‘=’ into ‘≠’ or a minus sign.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters after move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, each affected character must still correspond to a recognized Roman numeral or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after each proposed relocation, before accepting the move.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from V must not leave a single diagonal, which is not a numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid orientation mismatches
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their orientation; a vertical stick cannot become diagonal, and a horizontal cannot become vertical.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When choosing a stick to relocate, ensure the target shape requires the same orientation.
matchstick.example: A vertical stick from ‘+’ can become the stem of an ‘I’, but cannot be used to form a diagonal part of a ‘V’.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion only when resulting operator is valid
matchstick.principle: Changing an operator (e.g., ‘+’ to ‘-’) is allowed only if the new symbol is a legal operator in the puzzle.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick move would alter an operator; verify the new shape matches a permitted operator.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from ‘+’ yields ‘-’, which is valid.

matchstick.title: Recompute numeric values after transformation
matchstick.principle: After any stick relocation, recalculate the Arabic values of all numerals and re‑evaluate the arithmetic to confirm equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After finalizing a move, before submitting the answer.
matchstick.example: After turning ‘+’ into ‘-’ and adding an I, recompute RHS: 13 − 4 = 9, matching LHS.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick away turns it into a minus sign while providing a vertical stick for other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests a change of ±2 × operand, and a vertical stick is needed elsewhere.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ to the numeral ‘XII’ creates ‘XIII’ and changes ‘+’ to ‘-’, fixing the equation.

matchstick.title: Dual‑character stick relocation for balancing values
matchstick.principle: A single stick can be moved from one character to another, simultaneously decreasing the source’s value and increasing the destination’s value, useful for matching a numeric gap.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy equals the sum of a possible decrease in one character and an increase in another.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ (decreasing RHS by 8) to ‘XII’ (increasing it by 1) resolves a 7‑point gap.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick addition creates extra I (value +1)
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a numeral creates an additional ‘I’, raising its value by 1 without breaking other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a vertical stick is available (e.g., from a ‘+’) and the needed adjustment is exactly +1.
matchstick.example: Adding the vertical stick from ‘+’ to ‘XII’ yields ‘XIII’.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Model conflates stick identity with shape, ignoring the rule that orientation is fixed.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always check the orientation of the source stick and ensure the target character requires the same orientation.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Model seeks any stick to move and overlooks the rule that ‘=’ must stay unchanged.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never select a stick from the equality sign; treat it as immutable.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid character after move
matchstick.why_it_happens: Model focuses on numeric balance and forgets character validity.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every affected character matches a known numeral/operator.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: Model moves sticks without checking the operator set.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator is altered, confirm the new shape is either ‘+’, ‘-’, or ‘=’.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Model jumps to arbitrary stick moves instead of using arithmetic guidance.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Start by converting Roman numerals to Arabic, compute the gap, and let that guide the stick relocation.
